The OIG has documented several findings about medication‑carts that were left unlocked or unattended in patient‑care areas. Below are the reports that specifically cite this problem, together with the recommendation and the report link.

| Report (year) | Report number | Finding quoted in the OIG report | Recommendation (summarized) | Link |
|---------------|--------------|----------------------------------|------------------------------|------|
| 2015 | **15‑00606‑495** – Combined Assessment Program Review of the Battle Creek VA Medical Center (Michigan) | “We recommended that employees secure medication carts when not in use and that facility managers monitor compliance.” | Secure medication carts after each use and conduct weekly random checks until 100 % compliance for a 90‑day period. | <https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-battle-2> |
| 2014 | **13‑03653‑91** – Combined Assessment Program Review of the Atlanta VA Medical Center (Georgia) | “We recommended that processes be strengthened to ensure that medication carts are secured at all times and that compliance be monitored.” | Nursing staff must keep carts locked; non‑functional locks are being repaired or replaced; interim storage in a locked medication room; BCMA coordinator conducts routine rounding. | <https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-atlanta-va-1> |
| 2013 | **13‑00279‑156** – Combined Assessment Program Review of the VA Palo Alto Health Care System (California) | “We recommended that processes be strengthened to ensure that medication carts are secured at all times and that compliance be monitored.” | Nursing managers reinforce policy, distribute safety flyers, and conduct monthly audits of carts, medication rooms, and BCMA drawers until 100 % compliance. | <https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-va-palo-2> |
| 2014 | **14‑00689‑142** – Combined Assessment Program Review of the Orlando VA Medical Center (Florida) | “We recommended that processes be strengthened to ensure that medication/supply carts are secured at all times and that compliance be monitored.” | All staff must lock carts before leaving an exam room; one‑on‑one review and email communication were provided; service chiefs to conduct additional training. | <https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-orlando-va-0> |
| 2015 | **15‑00071‑158** – Combined Assessment Program Review of the West Palm Beach VA Medical Center (Florida) | “On the CLC‑N unit, two medication carts were unlocked and unattended.” (see recommendation 8) | Recommendation 8 required securing medication carts when not in use and monitoring compliance. | <https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-west-palm-2> |
| 2016 | **16‑00106‑211** – Combined Assessment Program Review of the Charlie Norwood VA Medical Center (Georgia) | “Three of seven patient‑care areas had unlocked medication‑cart drawers; expired medications; or undated, open multi‑dose vials.” | Employees must secure medication carts when not in use. | <https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-charlie-1> |
| 2021 | **20‑03593‑140** – Care and Oversight Deficiencies Related to Multiple Homicides at the Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center (West Virginia) | “In 2018, medication carts on ward 3A were not consistently secured as some were unlocked and unattended, and staff could use the same code to unlock medication carts throughout the facility.” | OIG recommended securing carts and restricting code access. | <https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/hotline-healthcare-inspection/care-and-oversight-deficiencies-related-multiple-homicides> |
| 2012 | **12‑03075‑52** – Combined Assessment Program Review of the Miami VA Healthcare System (Florida) | “We found several unsecured medications on top of a medication cart in an unlocked room being used as a medication room.” | Staff instructed to secure medications at all times; two locked carts ordered. | <https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-miami-va-1> |

**Data as of 2026‑11‑04** (the date of the OIG dataset used for these results).
